correctness.rationale: PASS: A one-sided purchaser configuration forces the entire side (n buyers); mixed purchaser counts p,q≥1 have exact necessary and sufficient feasibility 1≤p,q≤n-k, kp+q≥n, p+kq≥n. Sufficiency follows by independently covering recipients with distinct length-k cyclic nomination blocks. For fixed s=p+q, balanced p,q maximize min(p,q), yielding 2≤s≤2(n-k) and s+(k-1)floor(s/2)≥n. The inequality is monotone, with first even and odd feasible thresholds equal to the displayed a(n,k); the maximal s is feasible. k=n precludes mixed buyers. Fresh exhaustive exact recipient-subset coverage agreed on every (n,k) with 2≤n≤8 (35 pairs). The all-size theorem follows from the constructive inequalities, not enumeration.
